thread:
ben: rolled base image with nvidia-container-toolkit v1.13.1 into eu-west-1 at 09:05 UTC, now seeing containers fail to start on some GPU nodes
carla: how many nodes and what's the symptom?
ben: ~10 nodes; kubelet logs show failures resolving/binding vendor libs inside the init container. sample:
```
OCI runtime init failed: error mounting "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1": permission denied
failed to create symlink from /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: operation not permitted
```
alex: is this limited to that AZ or image variant?
ben: only eu-west-1. nodes were provisioned with an alternate host image that uses uid-mapped mounts (shiftfs) for rootless workflows. us-west-2 unaffected.
priya: could userns remap be blocking symlink creation inside the container mount namespace?
ben: looks like the toolkit's container-tool (nvidia-ctk) expects to be able to create symlinks or bind-mount host libs into the container filesystem; with shiftfs + propagation setup we can't create the symlink so the loader inside container doesn't find libcuda/libnvidia-ml
dan: side effect: auto-failover moved traffic cross-region, now increasing egress and on-call cost metric spiked
node-monitor-bot: alert: 10 GPU nodes NotReady in eu-west-1; impacted GPUs: 40 ; scheduling backlog: +18 pods
carla: urgent options: (1) revert base image to previous toolkit, (2) patch daemonset to mount host /usr/lib with hostPath, (3) cordon and drain affected nodes and reprovision without uid-mapping
alex: I can test approach (2) as a canary — add hostPath mounts for /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and /run/nvidia with mountPropagation HostToContainer and also set readOnly where safe
ben: tried that on one canary node: pod init passes but at runtime the CUDA loader complains about wrong SONAME paths. logs:
```
ldconfig: warning: /host-libs does not contain library cache
CUDA driver version mismatch: libcuda.so.1: version 'NVIDIA-GLIBCXX' not found
```
ben: implies the hostPath approach masked the symlink issue but exposed ABI/loader path differences — some hosts have lib paths under /usr/lib, others under /usr/lib/wrongarch (we have distro drift)
priya: impact assessment: serving capacity in eu-west-1 reduced by ~55% for GPU-backed prod routes; failover added ~12% latency on average for affected customers
carla: can we fast rollback the image? how long to produce and redeploy old image?
ben: building revert image to toolkit v1.12.0 now. estimated rebuild + push + canary deploy ~35-45 minutes. starting rollback pipeline and pausing rollout to other regions
infra-bot: incident INC-2026 created, severity: P2, assigned: ben, owner_ttl: 2026-11-09T11:00:00Z
dan: meanwhile we should cordon the worst nodes to avoid noisy failures and reduce autoscaler thrash
ben: cordoned 6 nodes; draining will move remaining pods to healthy hosts in-region when possible
carla: please draft customer-facing note for eu-west-1 ops and post to #customers-ops after Ben confirms canary success
ben: rollback image built and pushed at 09:40 UTC, initiating staged canary rollout (2 nodes)
node-monitor-bot: event: canary redeploy succeeded on 2 nodes; GPUs back online: +8
ben: after rollback, init containers now show successful bind mounts and ldconfig finds libnvidia-ml and libcuda inside container rootfs
carla: proceed with region-wide redeploy in waves; keep autoscaler conservative to avoid cross-region bursts
alex: followups: add a CI integ test that performs a toolkit init on uid-mapped host image matrix (kernels 5.15, 6.1, 6.4) and verifies lib probes succeed
dan: also add telemetry: a synthetic probe across all zones that runs `nvidia-smi -L` from an instrumented pod after each toolkit image rollout and alert on probe failures
priya: long-term: consider banning shiftfs/uid-map images from GPU fleet or enhance toolkit to avoid on-file symlink creation by using absolute hostPath mounts with consistent paths
ben: created ticket INFRA-1429 "handle toolkit lib mount + uid-mapped hostfs" with remediation options and checklist
carla: update: customer note posted and ops notified. I'll keep channel updated during the staged redeploy. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: incident INC-2026 status: mitigated -> rolling remediation, P2
ben: final status: rollback complete in eu-west-1 at 10:30 UTC, capacity restored to 98% ; scheduling backlog cleared. continuing follow-ups for CI and fleet policy
carla: closing thread once followups owned and alerts in place. thanks team.
